title: The Letter to the Galatians Timeline
sub: No Other Gospel · Justified by Faith, Not Works of the Law
desc: Paul's angriest letter, skipping his usual thanksgiving to confront churches deserting the true gospel for one requiring circumcision. Built around a public confrontation with Peter, an argument from Abraham's own faith, and the declaration that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free.

eras.label: Era One · Galatians 1
eras.name: No Other Gospel
eras.dates: Paul's angriest opening — no greeting-thanksgiving at all, straight into astonishment that the Galatians are deserting the gospel so quickly

events.title: Let Him Be Accursed — No Other Gospel
events.detail: Paul skips his usual thanksgiving entirely and goes straight to alarm: the Galatians are deserting the true gospel for a different one, and Paul pronounces a curse twice on anyone, even an angel, who preaches a contrary message.

verses.text: “Even if we, or an angel from heaven, should proclaim to you a gospel contrary to the gospel we have proclaimed to you, let him be accursed!” — repeated twice for emphasis.

events.title: A Gospel Received by Revelation, Not From Man
events.detail: Paul insists his gospel came directly from Jesus Christ, not from human teaching or a committee decision — the foundation for everything he argues in the rest of the letter.

verses.text: “I neither received it from man, nor was I taught it, but I received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ.”

events.title: Paul's Early Years — Persecutor, Then Preacher
events.detail: A rare autobiographical passage: Paul's zealous persecution of the church, his call, three years in Arabia before ever consulting Jerusalem, and a brief first visit where he met only Cephas and James.

verses.text: “When God… was pleased to reveal His Son in me… I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood… but I went away to Arabia.” — establishing his independence from the Jerusalem apostles from the very start.

eras.label: Era Two · Galatians 2
eras.name: Justified by Faith, Not Works of the Law
eras.dates: A private meeting with the Jerusalem pillars, a public confrontation with Peter, and the letter's doctrinal thesis stated outright

events.title: The Jerusalem Pillars Extend the Right Hand of Fellowship
events.detail: Fourteen years later, Paul lays his gospel before the Jerusalem leaders privately, refuses to let Titus be forced into circumcision, and receives full recognition from James, Cephas, and John — a division of mission fields, not doctrine.

verses.text: “James and Cephas and John, who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we might go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.”

events.title: Confronting Cephas at Antioch
events.detail: Paul recounts publicly opposing Peter to his face for withdrawing from table fellowship with Gentile believers once certain men from James arrived — a hypocrisy so contagious it swept up even Barnabas.

verses.text: “If you, being a Jew, live like the Gentiles and not like the Jews, how is it that you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?” — Paul's own recorded rebuke to Peter.

events.title: Justified by Faith — ‘I Have Been Crucified With Christ’
events.detail: Paul states the letter's central thesis in compressed form: no one is justified by works of the Law, only through faith in Christ — and describes his own identity as having died with Christ so that Christ now lives in him.

verses.text: “Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the Law but through faith in Jesus Christ… since by the works of the Law no flesh will be justified.”
“I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.”

eras.label: Era Three · Galatians 3
eras.name: Sons of Abraham Through Faith
eras.dates: An argument built entirely from the Old Testament — Abraham believed before the Law existed, so faith, not law, was always the point

events.title: Foolish Galatians — Did You Receive the Spirit by Faith or by Law?
events.detail: Paul asks a single pointed question: did their experience of the Spirit come from keeping the Law or from believing the message? Abraham himself was counted righteous by faith, centuries before the Law was given.

verses.text: “Just as Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness.”

events.title: Redeemed From the Curse of the Law
events.detail: Christ himself became a curse to redeem those under the Law's curse — and Paul makes a precise legal argument that a promise made to Abraham 430 years before the Law cannot be annulled by the Law that came later.

verses.text: “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us—for it is written, ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.’”

events.title: The Law as Tutor Until Christ
events.detail: Paul explains the Law's real, limited purpose — not to give life, but to guard and restrain until faith in Christ arrived, functioning like a household tutor whose job ends once the child comes of age.

verses.text: “The Law has become our tutor unto Christ, so that we may be justified by faith. But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.”

events.title: Neither Jew Nor Greek — All One in Christ
events.detail: The chapter closes in one of the New Testament's most sweeping statements of unity — baptism into Christ dissolves the ethnic, social, and gender categories that structured the ancient world, making everyone equally Abraham's heir.

verses.text: “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is no male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.”

eras.label: Era Four · Galatians 4
eras.name: From Slaves to Sons — Hagar and Sarah
eras.dates: Legal adoption imagery gives way to personal appeal, and then to an Old Testament story read as a live allegory

events.title: No Longer Slaves, but Sons — ‘Abba, Father’
events.detail: An heir under guardianship differs little from a slave until the appointed time — Paul applies this to salvation history: at the fullness of time God sent his Son, so believers receive adoption and the Spirit crying 'Abba, Father.'

verses.text: “God sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying, ‘Abba! Father!’ Therefore you are no longer a slave, but a son.”

events.title: A Personal Appeal — Paul's Own Illness Among Them
events.detail: Paul shifts from argument to raw personal emotion, recalling a bodily illness that first brought him to Galatia, the affection they once showed him, and his current perplexity and labor pains over their wavering.

verses.text: “My children, with whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you—but I could wish to be present with you now and to change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.”

events.title: The Allegory of Hagar and Sarah
events.detail: Paul reads Abraham's two sons — one by the slave woman Hagar, one by the free woman Sarah — as a live allegory of two covenants, identifying the demand for circumcision with slavery and freedom in Christ with the promised, free son.

verses.text: “Cast out the servant-woman and her son, for the son of the servant-woman shall not be an heir with the son of the free woman.” — quoting Genesis 21:10 as a direct word against the circumcision party.

eras.label: Era Five · Galatians 5
eras.name: Freedom, Not a Yoke of Slavery
eras.dates: Freedom defined against two opposite failures — legalism on one side, self-indulgence on the other

events.title: Stand Firm — A Little Leaven Leavens the Whole Lump
events.detail: Paul states the stakes of circumcision plainly — accepting it obligates a person to keep the whole Law and severs them from grace — and expresses a sharp, almost shocking wish about those pressuring the Galatians.

verses.text: “You have been severed from Christ, you who are being justified by law; you have fallen from grace!”

events.title: Freedom to Serve One Another in Love
events.detail: Freedom isn't a license for self-indulgence — Paul redirects it toward serving one another, summarizing the entire Law in a single command drawn from Leviticus.

verses.text: “The whole Law is fulfilled in one word, in this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

events.title: Walk by the Spirit — The Fruit of the Spirit
events.detail: One of the most quoted passages in Paul's letters: a list of the flesh's works set directly against the Spirit's fruit — not a rulebook, but the natural produce of a life led by the Spirit rather than the flesh.

verses.text: “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.”

eras.label: Era Six · Galatians 6
eras.name: Bear One Another's Burdens
eras.dates: Practical closing instructions, then Paul takes the pen himself for a final, large-lettered word

events.title: Restore Gently — Bear One Another's Burdens
events.detail: Spiritual believers are told to restore someone caught in sin gently, watching their own vulnerability, and to carry each other's burdens as a way of fulfilling the law of Christ — while each still bears his own load.

verses.text: “Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.”

events.title: Sowing and Reaping — Do Not Lose Heart in Doing Good
events.detail: A closing agricultural metaphor with real stakes: sowing to please the flesh reaps corruption, sowing to the Spirit reaps eternal life — and Paul urges perseverance in doing good before the harvest comes.

verses.text: “Whatever a man sows, this he will also reap. For the one who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption, but the one who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.”

events.title: Paul's Own Large Handwriting — Boasting Only in the Cross
events.detail: Paul takes the pen from his scribe to write the closing himself, in large letters, exposing the circumcision party's real motive as avoiding persecution — and states his own boast is the cross alone.

verses.text: “May it never be that I would boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.”
